newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares hover in tight range.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares hover in tight range.

text.p: Jordanian shares closed fractionally down on Tuesday in moderate trade as the official stock exchange index hovered around 149.5 points for the fifth day in a row.
"There's just no new factors driving this market at the moment," one broker said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index slipped back less than 0.1 percent to 149.49 points, barely changed since Monday, as shares worth 1.17 million dinars ($1.65 million) changed hands.
A slight fall in Livestock and Poultry, which has dominated trade all week, helped push the overall index down.
The shares rose briefly to a 12-month high of 0.96 dinars before slipping back to close at 0.93, down 0.01, after turnover worth 527,000 changed hands.
The stock has doubled in recent weeks and brokers say even board members have started selling their shares to cash in on the rise.
Banking shares accounted for the bulk of remaining trade, with troubled Amman Investment Bank falling to 0.36 dinars after reaching 0.40 during Tuesday's trade.
Middle East Investment Bank, which traders have linked to interest from a major French bank, slipped back 0.02 dinars to 1.17 dinars.
Declining shares outnumbered gainers by 21 to seven, while 19 closed unchanged from Monday.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange was unchanged on 82.88 points, 13.23 percent down from the same time last year.
